sections.h2: What should a seller know about Greene County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Greene County sits on the eastern edge of Tennessee, with Greeneville as its seat and largest town. It covers 624 square miles, of which 622 are land, so it is large by Tennessee standards. Settlers formed it in 1783 out of what was then Washington County, North Carolina, and it carries the name of Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene.

The land is mostly Ridge-and-Valley country. Bays Mountain forms much of the northern boundary with Hawkins County, while the far southeast corner climbs into the Bald Mountains along the North Carolina line. The Nolichucky River crosses the southern half and is held back by Nolichucky Dam south of Greeneville, which creates Davy Crockett Lake. Interstate 81 and US 11E carry most of the through traffic.

Greene County has one city, Tusculum, and the towns of Baileyton, Greeneville and Mosheim. Two public school systems serve it: Greeneville City Schools inside the Greeneville limits and Greene County Schools everywhere else. That split matters when you list a house, because buyers often ask which district a street falls in.

The Census Bureau lists these figures for the county:

  • 73,831 residents in July 2025, up 5.2 percent since April 2020
  • 33,581 housing units, with 77.1 percent lived in by their owners
  • $207,500 as the median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024
  • $56,194 median household income and 16.3 percent of people below the poverty line
  • 276 building permits issued in 2025

sections.h2: Which Greene County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two elected officials share the job. The Assessor of Property sets what each parcel is worth, and the Trustee sends the bills and takes the money. The county commission picks the rate. The Trustee's own website says the trustee does not decide the size of your bill.

The Trustee, Nathan Holt, works from the Greene County Government Administration Center at 401 Takoma Avenue, Suite 104, Greeneville, TN 37743. The phone is 423-798-1705 and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The Assessor of Property, Chuck Jeffers, is listed by the county technical assistance service at 401 Takoma Avenue, Suite 106, phone 423-798-1738.

The Town of Greeneville bills its own tax. Its Recorder's Office accepts and receipts the town's property tax payments, so a house inside the Greeneville limits produces two bills, one for the county and one for the town. The Comptroller notes that a city collecting official may be the city recorder, treasurer or the county trustee, so ask which applies to a given address in Mosheim, Baileyton or Tusculum.

sections.h2: How is a Greene County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
Multiply the assessed value by the tax rate and divide by 100. The Comptroller says the assessed value is the appraised value times a ratio set by state law: 25 percent for residential and farm property and 40 percent for commercial and industrial property.

The Trustee's page works a sample: an assessed value of $25,000 at a rate of $1.8731 per $100 comes to $468.28, which rounds to a $468 bill. The Trustee labels that figure an illustration. For a home appraised at $207,500, the Census median for the county, the assessed value would be $51,875, and the bill is that number times the current rate divided by 100. Ask the Trustee for this year's county rate and the town rate, since both are set by local bodies each summer.

Where the money goes is spelled out too. Property tax is the largest local tax feeding the county general fund, wheel tax comes second, and the school fund draws its biggest share from state education money, with local property tax and local sales tax next.

sections.h2: When is Greene County property tax due and how can I pay it?
sections.html:
The 2026 county bills were payable starting Monday, October 5, 2026, and they stay open without interest through the end of February 2027. On March 1 they turn delinquent and interest starts. Today is November 15, 2026, so the bill is already payable and nothing is late yet.

State law does not require the county to mail a notice. The Trustee sends one as a courtesy, and failing to get it does not excuse interest. If yours has not arrived, call 423-798-1705, and call the Assessor at 423-798-1738 to fix a mailing address.

Payment options listed by the Trustee:

  • In person at Suite 104 with cash, check, money order or card
  • By mail to the same address, with the stub and the receipt number written on the check (the postmark counts)
  • By phone at 1-833-591-7184, or online at tnproptax.com
  • In the payment slot just inside the main entrance of the Administration Center

Cards carry a 2.5 percent vendor fee and online ACH carries $1.25. Greene County does not receive these fees.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Greene County assessment?
sections.html:
Go first to the county Board of Equalization, which opens its yearly session on June 1. The state treats a disputed value as final unless it was taken to that county board, with a few listed exceptions. The Assessor's office is the contact for filing.

If the county board turns you down, the next stop is the State Board of Equalization. You have until August 1 of the tax year or 45 days after the county board's notice went out, whichever is later. An administrative judge hears the case and issues a written decision within 90 days of the hearing. The owner has to prove the correct value, and the state office takes calls at 615-401-7883.

The Comptroller's guidance on what persuades a judge:

  • Recent sales of similar homes, with differences in size, age, condition and location explained
  • A professional appraisal, whose author may be asked to testify
  • A stated value and the reasons for it, because saying the house is overvalued is usually not enough

Pay at least the part of the bill you do not dispute before March 1, and clear any older delinquent years, or the appeal can be delayed or dismissed.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Greene County homeowners use?
sections.html:
Tennessee reimburses part of the tax for low-income elderly and disabled homeowners, disabled veterans, and widows or widowers of certain disabled veterans. The 2026 limits are a maximum 2025 income of $38,470 for elderly and disabled applicants, with relief calculated on at most $33,600 of market value. Disabled veterans are measured on up to $175,000 of market value. You must own the home and live in it, and elderly applicants must be 65 by December 31, 2026.

This is a reimbursement and not an exemption, so you still pay the bill and then the state sends money back. The Greene County Trustee takes applications from the first Monday in October through the end of the following March and asks you to phone 423-798-1705 first to learn which papers to bring. The state brochure sets the final date at 35 days after the delinquency date, so confirm the exact day.

The local-option tax freeze for owners 65 and older is a separate program. Greene County does not appear on the Comptroller's list of 28 counties that have adopted it, so ask the Trustee whether anything has changed.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Greene County house sells?
sections.html:
The Trustee says taxes are usually prorated at closing and that the Trustee's office does not do the proration between buyer and seller. Your closing agent or title company works out each side's share, so look for it on the settlement statement.

A seller who owes back tax should ask the Trustee for a payoff figure early, because interest runs on every month after February. An owner who is selling quickly because of an inherited house, a vacancy or a stack of repairs can bring the tax balance to the title company and have it paid from the proceeds. Recording the deed and the state transfer tax of $0.37 per $100 are handled at the register of deeds when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the Greene County property tax rate?
faqs.a: Ask the Trustee at 423-798-1705, because the county commission and the Town of Greeneville each set a rate every year and the figure changes. The Trustee's formula is assessed value times rate divided by 100, with homes assessed at 25 percent of appraised value.

faqs.q: When do Greene County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. The 2026 bills were payable from October 5, 2026 and carry no interest through the end of February. After that, interest is charged until the balance is paid.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Greene County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor of Property at 423-798-1738. The office is at 401 Takoma Avenue, Suite 106 in Greeneville. It handles value questions, mailing addresses and the path to the county Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Can I get a tax break in Greene County if I am over 65?
faqs.a: Yes, through the state relief program if your 2025 income was $38,470 or less and you own and live in the home. The Trustee takes applications. The local tax freeze is offered only in counties that adopted it, and Greene County is not on the state list.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller pay the Greene County property tax at closing?
faqs.a: Both, by proration. The Trustee says taxes are typically prorated at closing, and the title company or closing agent works out the split. The Trustee's office does not do it.
